_about: Moat scorecard (question 4: how durable is the competitive advantage?) -> data/moat_scorecard.json. See scripts/moat_scorecard.py for the scoring.

AAPL.why: iOS ecosystem lock-in (iCloud, iMessage, apps, accessories) and the strongest consumer brand in tech; App Store links developers and users.
AAPL.risk: App Store fee rulings (EU DMA, US Epic case) and slower upgrade cycles.

MSFT.why: Office, Windows, Azure and Entra are embedded in company IT; moving off is costly and risky. Hyperscale cloud is a scale game few can play.
MSFT.risk: AI spending needs to earn its cost; price competition in cloud.

GOOGL.why: Search and YouTube: more users bring more advertisers and better data; Android and Chrome distribution; lowest cost to serve at scale.
GOOGL.risk: AI answers changing search habits; US antitrust remedies on default deals.

AMZN.why: Marketplace links sellers and Prime buyers; logistics network and AWS scale give a cost edge rivals can't match.
AMZN.risk: Heavy AI and logistics capital spending; retail margins stay thin.

NVDA.why: CUDA software and developer base make switching costly; leading chip designs and networking sold as full systems.
NVDA.risk: Customers' own chips (TPU, Trainium) and AMD; spending cycles in AI data centres.

AVGO.why: Custom AI chips and networking designed in for years; VMware is deep in company data centres; many niche chips with few rivals.
AVGO.risk: Depends on a handful of hyperscaler customers; VMware customers unhappy with price rises.

LLY.why: Patents on tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) and a deep obesity pipeline; manufacturing scale in a supply-constrained market.
LLY.risk: Price pressure on GLP-1s and new rivals (oral drugs, Novo, generics of older drugs).

ADBE.why: Photoshop, Acrobat and Creative Cloud are the industry standard; file formats and training lock users in.
ADBE.risk: AI image and video tools (Canva, Figma, open models) lowering the bar for casual users.

APP.why: Ad network data and the AXON model improve with more apps and advertisers; mediation tool is widely installed.
APP.risk: Short track record outside gaming; platform rule changes by Apple and Google; short-seller claims on data use.

FICO.why: The FICO score is written into lender, investor and regulator processes; mortgage rules required it for decades.
FICO.risk: FHFA allowing VantageScore for mortgages; push-back on price rises.

APA.why: Oil and gas producer: price taker with no lasting edge apart from some low-cost Egypt and Permian acreage.
APA.risk: Oil and gas prices; reserve replacement.

DECK.why: HOKA and UGG brands with pricing power and growing direct sales.
DECK.risk: Fashion cycles; running shoe competition (On, Nike); tariffs.

INCY.why: Jakafi and Opzelura patents and a specialist dermatology and blood-cancer franchise.
INCY.risk: Jakafi patent expiry around 2028; pipeline must replace it.

MKC.why: Leading spice brand and shelf space; supplies flavours to food makers who rarely switch recipes.
MKC.risk: Store brands; volume weakness; commodity and tariff costs.

EXPE.why: Two-sided travel marketplace with hotel supply and loyalty programme, number two to Booking.
EXPE.risk: Google and AI agents taking the booking front door; heavy marketing spend.

BKNG.why: Largest hotel marketplace, especially independent hotels in Europe: more travellers draw more properties and the other way round.
BKNG.risk: Google and AI agents; EU DMA rules on parity clauses.

INTU.why: TurboTax and QuickBooks hold years of user data and accountant workflows; small firms rarely switch books.
INTU.risk: Free government tax filing; AI tax tools.

ADSK.why: AutoCAD and Revit are the standard file formats in design and construction; training and project files lock users in.
ADSK.risk: Slow construction cycle; cloud rivals in specific niches.

TPR.why: Coach brand with pricing power among younger buyers.
TPR.risk: Fashion cycles; reliance on one brand after the Capri deal failed.

VEEV.why: Life-science CRM and Vault are built into drug companies' regulated processes; few vendors know the niche.
VEEV.risk: Salesforce's rival life-science cloud; slower pharma spending.

MNST.why: Monster brand plus Coca-Cola bottler distribution worldwide.
MNST.risk: Celsius and new energy brands; health rules on caffeine.

ALLE.why: Schlage, Von Duprin and LCN specified into building plans; master key systems keep buildings with one maker.
ALLE.risk: Slower non-residential building; electronic lock rivals.

FTNT.why: Own security chips give a cost edge in firewalls; the Security Fabric ties products together.
FTNT.risk: Firewall refresh cycles; cloud security rivals (Palo Alto, Zscaler).

RMD.why: Leader in sleep apnoea masks and devices with connected-care software used by doctors and suppliers.
RMD.risk: GLP-1 drugs reducing apnoea; Philips returning to the US market.

V.why: Card network: more cardholders bring more merchants and the other way round; global acceptance and very low cost per transaction.
V.risk: Swipe-fee rules (Credit Card Competition Act); real-time payment systems and stablecoins.

FIX.why: Scale and skilled labour in mechanical contracting; modular building for data centres.
FIX.risk: Project business: data-centre spending cycle and labour costs.

MA.why: Card network: more cardholders bring more merchants and the other way round; global acceptance and very low cost per transaction.
MA.risk: Swipe-fee rules; real-time payment systems and stablecoins.

CTAS.why: Densest uniform and facility-services route network: each extra customer on a route costs little.
CTAS.risk: Slower hiring; UniFirst or Vestis competing on price.

DXCM.why: Continuous glucose monitors: patents and doctor and insurer relationships in a two-player market with Abbott.
DXCM.risk: Abbott price competition; quality issues and recalls.

IDXX.why: Vet clinics install IDEXX analysers and buy its test consumables for years; the largest reference lab network.
IDXX.risk: Fewer vet visits; Zoetis and Antech in diagnostics.

VRSN.why: Sole operator of .com and .net under a government contract; price rises allowed by contract.
VRSN.risk: Contract terms set by ICANN and the US government; flat domain volumes.

NDAQ.why: Exchange listings and trading plus financial software (Verafin, Adenza) that banks embed.
NDAQ.risk: Trading volume cycles; integration of acquisitions.

MCO.why: One of two dominant credit raters: issuers need a Moody's rating for investors to buy their bonds.
MCO.risk: Bond issuance cycles; regulation of raters.

SPGI.why: Credit ratings (duopoly with Moody's), S&P 500 index licences and Platts price benchmarks.
SPGI.risk: Bond issuance cycles; low-fee index rivals.

NFLX.why: Largest paid subscriber base spreads content cost over more users than any rival streamer.
NFLX.risk: YouTube and free video take viewing time; content costs.

CBOE.why: Owns the SPX and VIX option contracts; liquidity draws traders, which draws more liquidity.
CBOE.risk: Volume cycles; rivals listing copies of index options.

GRMN.why: Leader in niche devices (fitness, outdoor, aviation, marine) with brand and engineering depth.
GRMN.risk: Apple Watch and smartphones; slower consumer spending.

FDS.why: Financial data terminal built into analysts' workflows and spreadsheets.
FDS.risk: Bloomberg and LSEG; AI tools; fewer seats as banks cut staff.

CRM.why: Largest CRM; customer data and custom workflows make it hard to leave.
CRM.risk: AI agents changing how software is priced (per seat); slower growth.

HWM.why: Jet-engine parts certified for each engine; few qualified suppliers and long contracts.
HWM.risk: Aircraft production problems at Boeing and engine makers.

ADP.why: Payroll is mission-critical and painful to move; largest scale in payroll and HR outsourcing.
ADP.risk: Cloud HR rivals (Workday, Paycom, Rippling); job market slowdown.

AME.why: Many niche electronic instruments that are small costs to customers but critical, with few competitors each.

AXP.why: Closed-loop network with wealthy cardholders that merchants want; premium brand and rewards.
AXP.risk: Credit losses in a downturn; rewards card competition from Chase.

SHOP.why: Merchants build their store, payments and apps on Shopify; app partners add to its value.
SHOP.risk: Amazon and marketplace rivals; spending on AI commerce.

PYPL.why: Large two-sided checkout network and Venmo, though rivals (Apple Pay) are eating share.
PYPL.risk: Apple Pay and card-wallet checkout; low-margin processing growth.

XYZ.why: Square seller tools and Cash App, which links users and sellers.
XYZ.risk: Fierce competition in point-of-sale and consumer finance; credit risk.

ADYEY.why: Single global payments platform built in-house gives a cost and reliability edge for large merchants.
ADYEY.risk: Price competition from Stripe and banks; volume slowdown at large clients.

FISV.why: Bank core systems and Clover are deeply embedded, but Clover growth has disappointed.
FISV.risk: Execution reset in 2025; competition in merchant acquiring.

CRCL.why: USDC is the second-largest stablecoin with growing use in payments.
CRCL.risk: Income depends on interest rates and on Coinbase sharing; Tether and bank stablecoins.

SPG.why: Owns top-tier malls and outlets that are hard to replicate.
SPG.risk: Online shopping and weaker tenants; interest rates.

META.why: 3+ billion users across Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp: users draw advertisers and friends draw friends.
META.risk: TikTok competition; very large AI and Reality Labs spending.

TT.why: Leading commercial HVAC brand with service contracts and data-centre cooling know-how.

RL.why: Global luxury lifestyle brand with improving pricing power.
RL.risk: Fashion cycles; China and US consumer spending.

ROST.why: Off-price buying and low-cost stores let it sell below department stores at a profit.
ROST.risk: TJX and Burlington; tariffs on imported goods.

GDDY.why: Small businesses keep their domains, sites and email with the provider they started with.
GDDY.risk: AI site builders; price competition from Squarespace and Wix.

FAST.why: On-site vending machines and branches near customers give a service and cost edge in industrial supplies.
FAST.risk: Industrial slowdown; Grainger and Amazon Business.

SYK.why: Mako robot ties surgeons to Stryker implants; broad hospital relationships.
SYK.risk: Hospital budgets; pricing pressure in implants.

CMG.why: Strong brand and efficient kitchens in fast-casual dining.
CMG.risk: Low switching costs for diners; food and labour inflation.

KLAC.why: Dominant share in chip inspection and measurement tools; chip makers' processes are tuned to its machines.
KLAC.risk: Chip equipment cycles; China export rules.

CME.why: Main US futures exchange: liquidity in rates, equity and commodity futures draws traders; clearing ties them in.
CME.risk: New futures exchanges (FMX, crypto venues); volume cycles.

STE.why: Sterilisation equipment and consumables installed in hospitals and outsourced sterilisation for device makers.

WDAY.why: HR and finance system of record for large companies; switching is a multi-year project.
WDAY.risk: Seat-based pricing under AI; slower hiring at customers.

BR.why: Processes most US proxy votes and shareholder communications; few alternatives.
BR.risk: Regulatory change to proxy rules; slower trading volumes.

MSI.why: Public-safety radio networks and 911 software are built in for decades.
MSI.risk: Government budgets; FirstNet and broadband alternatives.

BKR.why: Gas turbines and LNG equipment with few global competitors; oilfield services are competitive.

RSG.why: Owns landfills and dense collection routes; new landfills are almost impossible to permit.
RSG.risk: Waste volume slowdown; fuel and labour costs.

WAB.why: Locomotives and rail parts in a market with very few makers; large installed base needs parts and service.
WAB.risk: Rail spending cycle; integration of acquisitions.

MRVL.why: Custom AI chips and optical networking designed into hyperscaler data centres.
MRVL.risk: Competition from Broadcom; dependence on a few customers.

LULU.why: Athleisure brand with loyal customers, now under pressure.
LULU.risk: Alo, Vuori and others; US sales decline.

RDDT.why: Community content draws users and AI data-licensing deals.
RDDT.risk: Depends on Google search traffic; early in ad monetisation.

CF.why: Low-cost US natural gas gives its nitrogen plants a cost edge over Europe and Asia.
CF.risk: Fertiliser price cycles; US gas price rises.

EME.why: Scale and skilled labour in electrical and mechanical contracting.
EME.risk: Project business: construction and data-centre cycle.

HST.why: Owns upper-end hotels in good locations; hotels are a competitive business.

LII.why: Direct-to-dealer distribution of home HVAC with strong dealer relationships.

NEM.why: Largest gold miner with some low-cost mines; gold price taker.
NEM.risk: Gold price; mine costs and execution.

REGN.why: Strong in-house research (Dupixent, Eylea) and antibody platform.

ZTS.why: Largest animal-health company with broad vet relationships; its patented dermatology drugs (Apoquel, Cytopoint) are losing share to new rivals and first generics.
ZTS.risk: US companion-animal sales -8% and dermatology -16% in Q3 2026 with 2026 organic growth reset to -2% to -1%; Librela safety concerns.

MO.why: Marlboro brand and pricing power in a shrinking US cigarette market.
MO.risk: Volume decline of 8-10% a year; regulation; weak position in vapes.

HAS.why: Owns brands like Magic: The Gathering, Monopoly and Dungeons & Dragons; digital games licensing.
HAS.risk: Toy demand; tariffs on imports from China.

BMY.why: Patents on Eliquis and Opdivo, but these expire around 2028.
BMY.risk: Patent cliff on its largest drugs; pipeline must fill the gap.

NRG.why: Large retail electricity customer base in Texas and power plants; regulated markets limit rivals.

FIS.why: Bank core and payment systems that banks rarely replace.
FIS.risk: Execution after selling Worldpay and buying issuer processing.

PG.why: Category-leading brands (Tide, Pampers, Gillette) with the largest ad and R&D budgets and retailer shelf power.
PG.risk: Store brands and price-sensitive shoppers; volume has been flat.

KO.why: The world's best-known drinks brand with an unmatched bottler distribution system.
KO.risk: Health trends against sugar, GLP-1 drugs and sugar taxes.

SHW.why: About 5,000 company-owned stores serving professional painters, who value service and stick with one supplier.
SHW.risk: Housing and industrial downturns; price-led growth.

JNJ.why: Patented drugs (Tremfya, Darzalex, Carvykti) plus surgical and cardiac devices that hospitals standardise on.
JNJ.risk: Stelara biosimilars, drug-price rules and talc litigation.

VLTO.why: Installed base of water-testing instruments (Hach) and coding printers (Videojet) that need its own consumables and service; ~60% of sales recurring.
VLTO.risk: Industrial slowdown in product-quality equipment; acquisitions dilute returns.

AMP.why: Long-lasting adviser-client relationships and sticky client assets; scale in advice, asset management and annuities.
AMP.risk: Market falls cut fee revenue; outflows at Columbia Threadneedle; adviser recruiting costs.

PPG.why: Specified coatings for car makers, aircraft and refinish shops (approval cycles and colour-matching systems) and global scale.
PPG.risk: Auto and industrial cycle; raw-material costs; weaker architectural paint.

EOG.why: Among the lowest-cost US oil producers, with premium drilling locations and its own marketing and gas pipelines.
EOG.risk: Oil and gas prices; shale inventory depletion.

PM.why: Marlboro outside the US, and IQOS and ZYN lead heated tobacco and nicotine pouches, backed by regulatory approvals and distribution.
PM.risk: Regulation and excise taxes; currency; competition in pouches.

DLTR.why: Scale buying and a low-cost store network around a fixed-price-point format.
DLTR.risk: Tariffs, low-income shoppers under pressure, competition from Walmart and Temu; multi-price rollout.

AMGN.why: Patents on Repatha, Evenity and Tezspire, plus biologics manufacturing scale.
AMGN.risk: Biosimilars for Prolia/Xgeva and later Enbrel; MariTide trial results.

INVA.why: Royalty rights on GSK's Relvar/Breo and Anoro inhalers and patents on its hospital drugs (Giapreza, Xerava, Zevtera).
INVA.risk: Inhaler royalties end as generics and patent expiries arrive; hospital-drug launches may not fill the gap.

CTRE.why: Long triple-net master leases with rent escalators and close ties to regional nursing operators; low cost of capital for its niche.
CTRE.risk: Operator failures, Medicaid and Medicare rate cuts, dilution from share-funded buying.

CVSA.why: Accredited nursing, medical and veterinary schools (Chamberlain, Ross, AUC) whose clinical placements and licensing approvals take years to copy.
CVSA.risk: US student-aid rules, enrolment cycles, lawsuits over Walden.

QLYS.why: Cloud platform embedded in customers' security and compliance processes; one agent feeds many modules, so customers rarely switch.
QLYS.risk: Platform rivals (CrowdStrike, Microsoft, Tenable) bundle vulnerability management.

LAUR.why: Leading private-university brands in Mexico and Peru with campuses, accreditations and employer ties built over decades.
LAUR.risk: Currency, local politics and education rules; cheaper online rivals.

IDCC.why: One of the largest wireless and video patent portfolios, licensed to most big phone makers under long contracts.
IDCC.risk: Licence renewals end in litigation, which can delay cash for years; patent courts and rules.

LMAT.why: Leader in small vascular-surgery niches that large med-tech companies ignore, with its own surgeon-facing sales force and tissue processing.
LMAT.risk: Recalls and regulation (EU MDR), hospital budgets, overpaying for acquisitions.

BOX.why: Content and permissions of large companies stored and shared in Box, with hundreds of app integrations; costly to move.
BOX.risk: Microsoft SharePoint/OneDrive and Google bundled for free; seat cuts.

ACIW.why: Core payment switches (BASE24) and real-time payment software run inside banks for decades; replacement is risky and slow.
ACIW.risk: Bank IT budgets, lumpy licence deals, cloud rivals and FIS/Fiserv.

ALL.why: Second-largest US home and auto insurer: the Allstate brand, a large agency force and scale in claims data and advertising.
ALL.risk: Catastrophe losses, auto claim inflation, state rate approvals; direct and price-comparison competitors (Progressive, GEICO).

HIG.why: Leading small-business insurer with automated underwriting and deep agent relationships, plus a top group-benefits franchise.
HIG.risk: Softer commercial prices, reserve charges on older liability years, catastrophes.

AIZ.why: Protection plans run inside the systems of large phone carriers, retailers and car dealers for years; lender-placed insurance is a niche with few rivals.
AIZ.risk: Losing a large carrier client, fewer phone upgrades, hurricanes in Global Housing.

MRSH.why: The largest insurance broker: global reach, data and specialist teams that large clients and insurers rely on; clients rarely switch broker.
MRSH.risk: Softer insurance prices, private-equity-backed brokers bidding for talent and deals, consulting cycles.

WTW.why: One of three global brokers, plus a leading pensions and benefits consultancy embedded in clients' HR and actuarial work.
WTW.risk: Softer insurance prices; Aon and Gallagher gaining scale; pension-consulting decline.

NMIH.why: One of six US mortgage insurers approved by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac; risk-based pricing engine and the lowest cost base among peers.
NMIH.risk: Housing downturn, GSE capital rules and possible privatisation, price competition.

UVE.why: Long-standing Florida homeowners insurer with its own claims and policy services and a large agent network.
UVE.risk: A major Florida hurricane; reinsurance costs; Florida politics and regulation.

PLMR.why: Specialist in earthquake and niche property lines that larger insurers avoid, with tailored underwriting data and a fronting platform.
PLMR.risk: A large California earthquake, reinsurance prices, new competitors in its niches.

PLGO.why: Specialty (re)insurance underwriting from Bermuda; little public record to judge an edge.

CRVL.why: Claims and bill-review software and networks embedded in employers' and insurers' workers' compensation processes; long client relationships.
CRVL.risk: Employment cycles, health-plan contracts, competition from larger claims administrators.

SLDE.why: Low-cost, technology-led Florida homeowners insurer that grows by taking policies from Citizens and failed insurers.
SLDE.risk: A major hurricane; reinsurance costs; Citizens depopulation slowing.

HG.why: Specialty insurance at Lloyd's and in the US plus reinsurance from Bermuda; Two Sigma manages part of its investments.
HG.risk: Catastrophes, softening reinsurance prices, investment swings.

HCI.why: Florida homeowners insurer with its own policy and claims software (Exzeo), which keeps costs low.
HCI.risk: A major Florida hurricane; reinsurance costs; Florida politics.

ESNT.why: One of six US mortgage insurers approved by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, with a reinsurance arm and a strong capital position.
ESNT.risk: Housing downturn, GSE capital rules and possible privatisation, price competition.

UFCS.why: Regional commercial insurer with long independent-agent relationships in the Midwest.
UFCS.risk: Reserve charges, catastrophes, larger and better-priced competitors.

SKWD.why: Specialty and E&S niches (captives, accident and health, agriculture, surety) where underwriting expertise matters more than size.
SKWD.risk: Casualty reserve charges, integrating Apollo, softer E&S prices.
